Telnet service is open: Open the device's settings page in a web browser (the address is often on a sticker on the device or in its manual).
Log in with the device's admin account.
Find the Telnet setting. It is usually under Advanced, Management or System.
Turn Telnet off and save the change.
Come back here and press Check again.
FTP service is open: Open the device's settings page and log in as admin.
Find the FTP or file sharing setting.
If you don't need FTP at all, turn it off.
SMB file sharing is reachable: If this is a computer, make sure its Windows or system updates are installed.
Ask your IT support whether this device should share files with the whole network.
If not, block file sharing from the device's firewall settings or limit it to specific computers.
Remote Desktop (RDP) is reachable: Ask your IT support whether remote desktop is needed on this computer.
If not needed: open Settings, find Remote Desktop, and turn it off.
If needed: make sure only trusted people can reach it, and that it asks for a password on every login.
VNC remote desktop is reachable: Open the VNC or remote-access program on the device.
Set a strong password, or turn the service off if nobody uses it.
Database port is reachable on the networ: This is usually a server. Ask your IT support to restrict the database to the local machine.
Make sure the database requires a password.
Press Check again once IT has made the change.
UPnP/SSDP service is reachable: Open your router's settings page (usually http://192.168.0.1 or tplinkwifi.net).
Log in with the router's admin account.
Find UPnP under Advanced or NAT settings and turn it off.
Web admin or alternate HTTP port is open: Open the device's admin page (the address is shown in the device list).
Log in and change the default password if you have not already.
If the admin page does not need to be reachable from the network, ask IT to restrict it.
Unencrypted HTTP is served: Turn on HTTPS (sometimes called SSL or secure web access).
Turn on the option to redirect HTTP to HTTPS, if available.
Outdated OpenSSH version: Install the device's system updates. On Linux: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade.
If the device is not a Linux computer, check its manufacturer's support page for updates.
Outdated Apache httpd version: Update the web server through the system's software updates (on Linux: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade).
If you are not sure how, ask your IT support to update it.
